bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read in `pixReadMemBmp`, not the older heap-use-after-free label carried in the ARVO metadata. The live staged ARVO image source is leptonica revision `95405007f7ebf7df69f13475b3259179cdc4ec12`, whose `pixReadMemBmp` still trusts signed BMP header sizes during colormap parsing. After the fuzzer consumes its 6-byte angle/x_center/y_center prefix, the remaining 59 bytes are parsed as a BMP slice with `bfOffBits = -13`, `biSize = -224`, `width = 34`, `height = -2`, `depth = 8`, and `biSizeImage = 0`. `pixReadMemBmp` normalizes the negative height to `2`, computes `fdatabpl = 36`, derives `cmapbytes = -13 - 14 - (-224) = 197` and `cmapEntries = 49`, and the later size check still passes because `59 == -13 + 36 * 2`. It then allocates a 196-byte colormap buffer and executes `memcpy(cmapBuf, cdata + BMP_FHBYTES + ihbytes, 196)` with `ihbytes = -224`, so the copy source points 210 bytes before the 59-byte BMP slice and reads before the testcase allocation. The staged patch's decisive obligation is the missing info-header-size validation: rejecting `ihbytes` outside the valid BMP header set would stop this witness before the colormap copy.

evidence_note: The staged `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` both show `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 196` in `pixReadMemBmp -> pixReadMem -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`. ARVO metadata still points at leptonica commits `50c3c353... -> 7a74abcd...` and labels the issue `CWE-416`, but the live staged ARVO image source is revision `95405007f7ebf7df69f13475b3259179cdc4ec12`; this GT follows the staged source and saved crash trace, and uses the metadata patch only as supporting evidence for the missing `ihbytes` validation obligation.

source.description: First project-side materialization of an attacker-controlled signed size field used by the vulnerable colormap math.
source.value_from: After `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` consumes the 6-byte prefix `20 ff 20 20 20 20`, the remaining 59-byte slice begins with BMP magic `42 4d`. The file-header bytes at offsets 10-13 of that slice are `f3 ff ff ff`, and these statements store them as signed `offset = -13`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The BMP info-header size is read directly from attacker-controlled bytes and stored as signed `ihbytes = -224`, which later drives both the forged colormap length and the underflowed `memcpy` source pointer.
tainted_value_origin.note: The staged witness bytes at offsets 14-17 of the 59-byte BMP slice are `20 ff ff ff`, so the staged source reads `biSize` as signed `0xffffff20`.

root_cause.code:
cmapbytes = offset - BMP_FHBYTES - ihbytes;
cmapEntries = cmapbytes / sizeof(RGBA_QUAD);
root_cause.description: The parser combines signed `offset` and signed `ihbytes` without first validating that `ihbytes` is a legitimate BMP info-header size, turning malformed negative header values into a positive colormap length.
root_cause.note: For the staged witness this arithmetic yields `cmapbytes = 197` and `cmapEntries = 49`, so the parser arms the colormap copy instead of rejecting the malformed header. The staged patch fixes this witness-specific obligation by rejecting `ihbytes` outside `{40, 108, 124}` before these calculations.

sink.code:
memcpy(cmapBuf, cdata + BMP_FHBYTES + ihbytes,
       sizeof(RGBA_QUAD) * cmapEntries);
sink.description: Closest project sink to the ASan crash. The colormap copy reads 196 bytes from a source pointer computed from the unchecked negative `ihbytes`, which points before the testcase buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 196` in `__asan_memcpy`, with `pixReadMemBmp` at `src/bmpio.c:250:9` as the closest project frame and the first reported poisoned address 32 bytes to the left of the original 65-byte testcase allocation.

parser_admitted.description: The post-prefix slice has already been classified as `IFF_BMP`, so `pixReadMem` dispatches into `pixReadMemBmp` on the staged witness.
parser_admitted.note: After the fuzzer strips its 6-byte prefix, `findFileFormatBuffer(data, &format)` sees the remaining slice's `BM` magic and sets `format = IFF_BMP`. The same infoheader also carries `biCompression = 0`, so the uncompressed-BMP rejection inside `pixReadMemBmp` is not taken.

fine_trace.note: Using the attacker-controlled 59-byte BMP slice passed from `pixReadMem`, the parser reads `bfOffBits` as signed `offset = -13` from bytes `f3 ff ff ff`.
The first 4 bytes of the BMP infoheader are `20 ff ff ff`, so the staged source stores `ihbytes = -224`. No validity check has yet constrained this to any legal BMP info-header size.

The same attacker-controlled infoheader bytes materialize `width = 34`, `height = -2`, `depth = 8`, and `imagebytes = 0`. These values survive the early width/depth checks and feed the later height normalization and row-size arithmetic.
Negative height is accepted as a top-down BMP. The taken branch flips `height` from `-2` to `2`, which is the height later used in the row-stride and size checks.

fine_trace.code:
fdatabpl = 4 * ((1LL * width * depth + 31)/32);
if (imagebytes != 0 && imagebytes != fdatabpl * height)
fine_trace.note: With `width = 34`, `depth = 8`, and normalized `height = 2`, the parser computes `fdatabpl = 36`. Because `imagebytes == 0`, the equality check against `fdatabpl * height` is bypassed rather than rejecting the malformed header.

fine_trace.code:
cmapbytes = offset - BMP_FHBYTES - ihbytes;
cmapEntries = cmapbytes / sizeof(RGBA_QUAD);
fine_trace.note: Unchecked signed header sizes are combined here: `cmapbytes = -13 - 14 - (-224) = 197`, and integer division truncates that to `cmapEntries = 49`. The malformed negative `ihbytes` is thus converted into a positive colormap-copy length instead of being rejected.
The staged source only rejects negative or huge colormap counts. The forged `cmapEntries = 49` passes both checks, so the colormap path stays reachable.

fine_trace.code:
if (size != 1LL * offset + 1LL * fdatabpl * height)
    return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("size incommensurate with image data",
fine_trace.note: The global size-consistency rejection is also bypassed. Inside `pixReadMemBmp`, `size` is the 59-byte post-prefix slice, and `offset + fdatabpl * height` is `-13 + 36 * 2 = 59`, so the negative offset still satisfies the check.
Because `cmapEntries > 0`, the parser allocates `49 * 4 = 196` bytes for `cmapBuf`, fixing the destination extent of the upcoming colormap copy.

fine_trace.var: cdata + BMP_FHBYTES + ihbytes, sizeof(RGBA_QUAD) * cmapEntries, cmapBuf
fine_trace.code:
memcpy(cmapBuf, cdata + BMP_FHBYTES + ihbytes,
       sizeof(RGBA_QUAD) * cmapEntries);
fine_trace.note: This copy uses `ihbytes = -224` as a source-pointer offset and `cmapEntries = 49` as the byte-count multiplier. The source address becomes `cdata + 14 - 224 = cdata - 210`, which is 210 bytes before the 59-byte BMP slice (204 bytes before the original 65-byte testcase allocation), and `memcpy` attempts to read 196 bytes from there into the 196-byte `cmapBuf`. The saved ASan trace reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read at this statement, with stack `pixReadMemBmp -> pixReadMem -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

allocation_context.description: ASan reports that the invalid read ultimately targets the malloc-backed 65-byte libFuzzer testcase allocation that holds the staged `poc`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_19723 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/pix_rotate_shear_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 196` in `pixReadMemBmp` with stack `pixReadMem -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: pix_rotate_shear_fuzzer testcase (6-byte prefix plus BMP tail)
format.contract: The staged witness is exactly 65 bytes long. Its first 6 bytes are the harness-only prefix `20 ff 20 20 20 20`, which `pix_rotate_shear_fuzzer` consumes as `angle`, `x_center`, and `y_center`. The remaining 59 bytes begin with BMP magic `42 4d` and carry `bfOffBits = f3 ff ff ff (-13)`, `biSize = 20 ff ff ff (-224)`, `biWidth = 22 00 00 00 (34)`, `biHeight = fe ff ff ff (-2)`, `biBitCount = 08 00`, and `biSizeImage = 00 00 00 00`. In the staged `pixReadMemBmp`, those exact values yield normalized `height = 2`, `fdatabpl = 36`, `cmapEntries = 49`, and `size == offset + fdatabpl * height == 59`, so `memcpy(cmapBuf, cdata + BMP_FHBYTES + ihbytes, 196)` executes with a source pointer before the testcase buffer and triggers the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.
